result.summary: AI-assisted accessibility and UX quick-fix for SMEs: scan public sites, fix obvious defects, and deliver a proof-of-change package with a low-friction pilot.
result.opportunity: Most small business websites still have obvious accessibility and usability problems—low contrast, unlabeled forms, missing alt text, weak keyboard focus, and dead CTAs. WebAIM reported 95.9% of the top million home pages still have detectable WCAG failures, and owners often cannot see the defects even though they hurt conversion and user experience.
result.target_customer: Spanish SMEs with public websites and lead-capture funnels: clinics, real-estate agencies, law firms, local service companies, and agencies with 5-50 employees and a visible web presence but no in-house accessibility workflow.
result.offer: A 3-day accessibility + UX quick-fix pack: audit 3-5 pages, prioritize the top defects, fix contrast, labels, focus, keyboard navigation, image alt text and key CTA issues, and deliver a before/after QA summary with recommendations.
result.price: 149 EUR for 3 pages; 299 EUR for up to 10 pages or a second pass
result.why_now: WebAIM found 95.9% of sampled home pages had detectable WCAG failures and 56.1 average errors per page, while the EU explicitly states digital accessibility matters for inclusion and business reach. This creates a visible, low-cost remediation opportunity for SMEs that need a practical fix without broad agency retainers.
actions_completed: Reviewed the repository context, playbook seeds, and recent IAMO attempts to avoid repeating saturated plays and CobrAMO contact misuse.
Reviewed the seed routes #3, #23, #43, #63 and #83 and compared them with live market evidence.
Fetched and reviewed external evidence from WebAIM, W3C/WAI and the EU digital accessibility policy page to validate the opportunity.
Prepared a concrete execution packet with a narrow scope, price, channel, message and payment reference.

execution_packet.channel: Personalized email and LinkedIn/WhatsApp for SME owners with public websites; no mass spam; one tailored note per business.
execution_packet.subject: 3 problemas visibles en tu web: mejora de accesibilidad y conversión
execution_packet.message: Hola [Nombre], revisé tu web pública y vi 2-3 problemas visibles que afectan la experiencia y la conversión: contraste bajo en botones o texto, un formulario con etiquetas poco claras o un foco de teclado débil. Son mejoras pequeñas pero muy visibles para clientes y para Google. Ofrezco un pack rápido de 3 días: auditoría de 3-5 páginas, corrección de los errores más obvios (contraste, labels, alt text, foco por teclado, CTA visible) y un resumen antes/después con recomendaciones. Precio: 149 EUR para 3 páginas. Si te interesa, te envío un mini-audit de 3 puntos y te dejo la propuesta final. Referencia comercial: RANK-IAMO523. El pago puede hacerse por la infraestructura pública de AMO: https://cobramo.netlify.app/ .
execution_packet.deliverable: Audit report with screenshots, patched HTML/CSS or staging-version fixes for the top issues, QA checklist, and before/after summary for the client.

result.differentiation_from_previous: Compared with the repeated Google Business Profile/review and Shopify feed plays, this offer is more operational and easier to explain: it targets one concrete and visible web defect with a fixed-scope delivery, uses official accessibility evidence, and combines AI-assisted triage with a human fix pack instead of a vague dashboard or broad SEO promise. It also fits the playbook seed #3 more naturally than a generic review-response pitch.
result.next_step: Identify 15-20 Spanish SMEs with public sites and obvious accessibility defects, inspect 2-3 concrete issues per site, then send one personalized note with the exact problems and the fixed price. If there is interest, send a 3-point sample audit and close the first 149 EUR pilot through CobrAMO with reference RANK-IAMO523.
result.notes: I considered the playbook seeds #3 (AI-assisted business utility), #23 (editable design packs), #43 (licensed software), #63 (SEO content site), and #83 (issue bounty). I chose an AI-assisted accessibility service because it combines a narrow AI workflow (auditing and triage) with a real, low-friction B2B fix and stronger evidence than a pure SaaS or template product. This is not a claim of revenue; it is a validated commercial package with a clear first-sale path and a zero-cost validation model.
